PullRequest.Title: test: revert browser-tools HTTP fixture
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/issues/3878

Reverts #336352 (`2302cc68e96b866a7e2ece80c9b134d7a3de7ed7`).

## Why

The HTTP-fixture change exposed a Windows Remote integration failure in [build 474234](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/a6d41577-0fa3-498e-af22-257312ff0545/_build/results?buildId=474234&view=logs&j=471dc74f-2452-533b-c058-e43cd1b98abf&t=ecf28f1e-60ae-500a-a6b3-8a0fe6542e51): `Open a page from the web` timed out after 60 seconds while opening the fixture's tunnel.

The test resolver requested a local port adjacent to the remote fixture's port; Windows rejected that bind with `EACCES`, and the tunnel creation promise did not settle.

## Change

Restore the test exactly to its pre-#336352 version, removing the HTTP fixture and tunnel setup. No resolver changes or unrelated tests are included.

This is a rollback, not a DNS fix. It restores navigation to Google, so the original external-DNS failure tracked in microsoft/vscode-engineering#3817 remains a separate follow-up.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed URL and fully awaited network call path are explicit, as is the 30-second navigation bound. The exact healthy-network delay and number of Google subresources vary, which limits severity, but the new external boundary and its critical-path placement are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: DNS lookup, TCP/TLS setup, the HTTPS response, and any page subresource requests made by the integrated browser
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One cold public navigation is added to each execution of this suite; that cost repeats across the Electron/remote OS test jobs, and a blocked endpoint can hold each invocation for the 30-second browser navigation timeout.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased integration-test latency and avoidable long stalls/timeouts on offline, DNS-restricted, or rate-limited runners.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The changed test navigated to an in-process loopback HTTP server. In non-remote Electron runs it performed no public DNS/TLS request; only remote runs additionally opened a tunnel.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The test now awaits `open_browser_page` for `https://google.com/` in every non-web suite run, moving a public network load onto the test's critical path.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 265 replaces the deleted `http://127.0.0.1:${address.port}/` invocation with an awaited `https://google.com/` invocation, introducing the public-network dependency on local test runs.
Findings.Title: Keep local browser-tool tests off the public network
Findings.Impact: A normal local or CI run must now reach Google before this test can complete. `OpenBrowserTool._openNewPage` awaits `createBrowserView`, whose `model.loadURL` reaches Electron's awaited `webContents.loadURL` with a 30-second timeout, so unavailable external networking can add tens of seconds and fail the suite; healthy runs still pay external DNS/TLS/page-load cost instead of loopback latency.
Findings.Evidence: The added line invokes `open_browser_page` with a public URL. The traced call path is `OpenBrowserTool._openNewPage` -> `BrowserViewWorkbenchService.createBrowserView` -> `BrowserViewModel.loadURL` -> `BrowserView.loadURL` -> awaited `webContents.loadURL`; `createBrowserView` caps this wait at 30,000 ms and only afterward waits for Playwright DOM readiness. The deleted hunk served the page from `127.0.0.1`, and the GitHub workflows compile/run these API integration tests on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the loopback fixture for non-remote runs, where no tunnel is needed, and use a separately bounded remote-only strategy (or skip this external-content case remotely) so fixing the tunnel hang does not make every integration run depend on Google.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: The prior remote-test path awaited creation of a localhost tunnel before invoking the browser tool, with no local timeout or cancellation around `workspace.openTunnel`; a failed Windows bind could leave the test blocked until Mocha's 60-second timeout.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: The remote browser-tools integration scenario could spend the full 60-second test timeout waiting for tunnel creation instead of opening the page.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The replacement invokes the browser tool directly and removes the local fixture and awaited tunnel setup, eliminating the tunnel-creation wait from the remote path.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base line 281 is the awaited `vscode.workspace.openTunnel` call inside the `vscode.env.remoteName` path, and the test has a 60,000 ms timeout. The review context identifies a Windows Remote run where the adjacent-port bind returned EACCES and the promise did not settle. Added line 265 directly invokes the browser tool without tunnel setup. `blame_base_line` resolves the old mechanism to commit 2302cc68e96b866a7e2ece80c9b134d7a3de7ed7.

Scenarios.Scenario: Local Electron API integration suite executes “Open a page from the web” on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The test awaits `invokeTool`; `OpenBrowserTool._openNewPage` awaits browser-view creation, `BrowserViewWorkbenchService.createBrowserView` awaits `model.loadURL`, and Electron awaits `webContents.loadURL` before Playwright waits for DOM readiness. The public fetch is therefore entirely on the test critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Public HTTPS navigation to Google, including DNS, TCP/TLS, response loading, and page subresources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One top-level public request sequence per suite execution plus site-controlled subresources; repeated across each integration job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The base test loaded one in-process loopback HTTP fixture; local runs had no public DNS/TLS dependency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fully awaited and bounded by the 30-second browser navigation timeout before the test can assert its result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and navigate an integrated browser view through workbench/main-process browser services.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One browser-view creation/navigation sequence for this test.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The base test invoked the same browser tool once for the loopback URL.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited, but the IPC cardinality itself is unchanged; only its URL/network target changed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One top-level navigation per suite execution, repeated independently across OS/jobs; Google may add subresource requests. No same-host tab exists elsewhere in this suite, and teardown closes editors, so effective cardinality is one cold navigation per run.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Tests in this suite execute serially. CI jobs can run in parallel, but each job independently waits for its own navigation; there is no limiter/coalescing across jobs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no test-level response cache or coalescing. Browser/DNS caches may be warm incidentally, but the repository has no other Google navigation in these tests and a fresh runner should be modeled as cold; failures are not negatively cached by the test.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added public URL, awaited call chain, timeout, and prior loopback target are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Healthy Google latency and subresource count vary by runner and geography, but restricted/offline runners can hold the explicit navigation timeout. This uncertainty limits severity, not mechanism confidence.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity regression: the diff newly blocks all local desktop integration runs on a public endpoint instead of loopback.

Scenarios.Scenario: Remote Electron API integration suite executes the same browser-tool test.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new path directly awaits the public browser navigation. The base path first awaited `workspace.openTunnel` with no local timeout, then loaded the tunneled loopback fixture.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a VS Code remote port tunnel for the fixture.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One tunnel-open request per remote execution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Present in the base revision and introduced by commit 2302cc68e96b866a7e2ece80c9b134d7a3de7ed7; this PR removes it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Previously awaited before navigation with only the enclosing 60-second Mocha timeout; now removed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Navigate the local integrated browser to `https://google.com/`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One top-level public navigation plus site subresources per remote suite execution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The browser loaded the forwarded loopback fixture after tunnel creation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One navigation per remote suite execution. The base path also created one loopback server and one tunnel per execution.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One test invocation and one tunnel/navigation sequence per remote runner; suite execution is serial, with independent CI runners potentially parallel.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new external request has no test-level cache. The removed tunnel had no reusable cache/coalescing because it was created and disposed inside each test.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both old tunnel await and new direct network await are explicit; the prior tunnel timeout is corroborated by review context and blame.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The direct public load can still vary or time out, but relative remote latency may improve substantially because the known non-settling tunnel boundary is gone.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate remote-path finding beyond the shared public-network issue; this PR also fixes the concrete tunnel-wait regression, which was recorded with `report_regression_fix`.

Scenarios.Scenario: Web integration execution of the API extension.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The entire `chat - browser tools` suite is skipped when `vscode.env.uiKind === vscode.UIKind.Web`, so the changed test is off the critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Zero executions of the changed invocation in web UI mode.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Not applicable because the suite is skipped.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the suite-level skip guard.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance impact in web integration runs.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the sole changed file and full diff. Submitted one low-severity finding for moving local CI navigation from loopback to a public endpoint, checked cleanup ownership through suite teardown, and recorded the removal of the remote tunnel wait as a regression fix.
